items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the environmental conservation law, in relation to control of
aquatic vegetation by means of a benthic barrier
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S894

SPONSOR: YOUNG
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the environmental conservation law, in
relation to control of aquatic vegetation by means of a benthic barrier

 
PURPOSE:

Authorizes the use of benthic barriers to control invasive aquatic
plants around residential docks or swimming areas.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Adds a new section 9-1711 to the Environmental Conservation Law, defin-
ing benthic barriers as a film of natural or synthetic matter, which is
gas permeable and anchored by means other than stone from the lake
bottom, for the sole purpose of controlling or suppressing aquatic vege-
tation around residential docks or swimming areas, and allowing for
their use between July first and October thirty-first each year without
being subject to the provisions of title five of article fifteen of this
chapter or General Permit GP-0-17-001.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Many lake residents currently use benthic barriers (mats) to control
invasive aquatic plants during the months of July-October. Recently, the
New York State Department of Environmental Conservation (DEC) has
proposed an onerous regulation that would force landowners to acquire a
permit in order to use benthic mats, citing concerns of mats covering
spawning beds and remaining in lakes after the season. This legislation
addresses DEC's concerns while also allowing lake residents to use
benthic mats in a manner that adheres to best practices, which they
currently follow, without the inconvenience of unnecessary regulation.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2018: S.5189-A/A.6722-A Committed to Rules
2017: S.5189/A.6722 Passed Senate

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

summary: Authorizes the use of benthic barriers, between July 1 and October 31, to control invasive aquatic plants around docks.
title: Authorizes the use of benthic barriers to control invasive aquatic plants around docks
